group.name: Are you updating from 1.6.2 or earlier?

plugin.name: Fresh install, or my box tokens are already off
plugin.description:
Carry on with the install.
1.6.3 changes how a costume's enchantments are given to you. The old way used a spell form that only existed while the game was running, so a bonus applied before you quit could not be taken back off on the next launch, and it stayed on your character. 1.6.3 fixes that, but it cannot clean up a bonus that is already stuck.
If you are on a fresh install, or you have taken your box tokens off and saved, there is nothing to do here.

plugin.name: Stop - I still have box tokens equipped
plugin.description:
This installs one text file and nothing else. No esp, no DLL, nothing that runs.
IMPORTANT: a FOMOD cannot refuse to install. The most it can do is install nothing useful. So if your mod manager asked whether to REPLACE your existing Costume Expansion FW, do not let it - install this as a new, separate mod, or the thing it replaces is the working install you are about to go back to.
Do this first, in the version you have now:
1. Run "cef av base". 2. Take off every box token. 3. Run "cef av diff". That lists what changed when the tokens came off, which is the part you want. ("cef av" on its own lists every actor value that anything is modifying, CEF's or not, so it cannot tell you which is which.) 4. Save. 5. Run this installer again.
If a bonus is still there after the tokens are off, it is already stuck and 1.6.3 will not remove it. "player.getavinfo health" tells you the number, and "player.modav health -N" takes it back off by hand. Do that before you update, so you are not guessing later which mod put it there.

plugin.name: Remove the old NPC add-on and VR patch first
plugin.description:
Up to 1.6.2 the NPC add-on and the VR build were separate downloads. They are both in this installer now.
If you still have them as separate mods, remove them before you install this. The VR patch matters most: it holds a DLL at the same path as this one, and depending on where it sits in your mod order it can put the old DLL back over the new one. Nothing in the installer can detect that for you, because the file has the same name either way.
Your boxes and settings are not in those mods and are not affected.

plugin.name: Skyrim Special Edition / Anniversary Edition
plugin.description: The normal build. Pick this unless you play in VR.

plugin.name: Skyrim VR
plugin.description:
Adds the VR notes. Nothing else changes.
Everything is identical across SE, AE and VR, the DLL included - it is one binary that works out which engine loaded it. Picking this only adds README_VR.txt, so if you install for SE and later move to VR you are not missing a file.
VR also needs SkyrimVRESL, and the in-game menu needs ImGui VR Helper. SkyUI VR on its own will not give you a CEF menu once the MCM is gone in 1.6.4.

plugin.name: NPC distribution
plugin.description:
Lets you publish a costume to NPCs and keep it on them across saves. Adds CostumeFW_NPC.esp and the carrier meshes the published and NPC-persist slots need.
Leave it off if you only dress your own character.

plugin.name: Enchantment passthrough (adds one full plugin)
plugin.description:
Keeps a costume's enchantments, armor rating and tempering working while the costume is in a box. This is on by default in CEF's settings, and from 1.6.3 it needs CostumeFW_Abilities.esp.
That plugin is NOT light (ESL). It takes one of your 254 load-order slots. It has to be a full plugin: the abilities live at fixed form IDs that your saves point at, and the light form-ID range is too small to hold enough of them.
If you would rather not spend the slot, untick this. CEF will then turn enchantment passthrough off and say so, rather than falling back to the old method - the old method is what put stuck bonuses on people's characters, and quietly using it again would be worse than not doing it at all. Your costumes still look exactly the same; they just stop carrying stats.
Once you have used this, leave it installed. Your saves refer to those form IDs, and removing the plugin strands whatever was applied.
